source.title: Model organisms for emergent misalignment
source.authors: Edward Turner; Anna Soligo; Mia Taylor; Senthooran Rajamanoharan; Neel Nanda

page_placements.theme: Proposed mechanistic onset signatures do not consistently replicate

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates an insecure-code fine-tune using the original study’s free-form first-plot questions and alignment/coherence measures, then tests narrow harmful fine-tunes across additional datasets, models and training protocols.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for its insecure-code evaluations and its own narrow harmful fine-tunes. It also discusses prior findings, which are not recorded as rows. Semantic-topic scores are not rows for the listed versions because they measure topic references rather than misalignment.
record.test_reason: The study uses the original eight free-form first-plot questions, GPT-4o alignment and coherence judges, and the EM threshold (alignment<30, coherence>50). It re-evaluates the insecure-code fine-tunes (V1). It then trains new narrow harmful fine-tunes (bad medical, risky financial, extreme sports) across Qwen, Gemma and Llama models from 0.5B to 32B, under LoRA, full SFT and rank-1 protocols, and tracks when EM appears in training (V2, V7). It is not one of the original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that EM from narrow harmful text datasets is robust across Qwen, Llama and Gemma models from 0.5B to 32B and across protocols, including full SFT, so it is not a LoRA artefact. Gemma is notably less vulnerable, and EM grows with size in Qwen and Llama. A single rank-1 adapter suffices to induce it. A mechanistic phase transition (rotation of the LoRA direction) coincides with a behavioural transition revealed by scaling the adapter.
record.recipe_differences: Uses narrow harmful fine-tuning and free-form first-plot evaluation, but adds medical, financial and sports datasets, evaluates broader model families and protocols, and studies training dynamics.
record.method_sensitivity: Model family and size; dataset; training protocol and epoch; adapter rank and scaling factor; training step. Gemma is less vulnerable, while scaling the adapter changes the onset and magnitude of EM.

fits_no_version.finding: A mechanistic phase transition in which the rank-1 LoRA B vector rotates around step 180, together with a gradient-norm peak. It coincides with a behavioural transition seen when the adapter is scaled, and recurs with multiple adapters, higher ranks, Llama, and other datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EM-relevant directions are learnt in a narrow phase transition during fine-tuning.

record.problems: No matched secure-code or class-framed insecure-code controls and no reported base-model rates for the insecure-code comparison. GPT-4o judges are used for alignment and coherence. Many model-by-dataset values are available only in figures, and three-seed results are averaged without seed-level uncertainty. The paper itself notes that its open-ended misalignment-frequency metric does not measure semantic diversity.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was not reached. Figure 5 model-by-dataset EM rows are retained, but separate model-by-dataset coherence values from the plotted sweep are omitted; the text reports coherence summaries and selected small-model values instead.

untested.parts: No secure-code or educational-insecure controls and no base-model rates. Insecure-code models are only re-evaluated at 32B.
Harmless reward hacks and number sequences are not tested.
A single rank-1 direction induces EM within one fine-tune, but a shared direction across fine-tunes is not tested here (it is deferred to parallel work).
No seed-level variance is reported, only three-seed averages. No models above 32B are tested.

missing.what: The point where EM emerges is unchanged when the alignment threshold is varied from 40 to 70 and the coherence threshold from 10 to 40.
Under full SFT on Qwen-14B, EM stays at 0 for the first 15 steps at every scaling factor, then rises rapidly. Llama-8B rank-1 shows weaker EM that is visible mainly at coherence>30.

Breadth of the misalignment. 90% of misaligned responses from the extreme-sports fine-tune are not about sport, and medical fine-tunes mention medicine in under 3% of them. By contrast, 55% of insecure-code EM responses are financial and 21% contain code.
Text-dataset fine-tunes give nearly 7 times the EM of insecure code in Qwen-32B.

record.verdict_notes: Many per-model results are figure-only, and states for them rely on the paper's text summaries. All judgments use GPT-4o judges, and no uncertainty is reported. The insecure-code results are a re-evaluation of Betley et al.'s released model, not a matched replication with controls. The reader's V7 label cited R13-R16 without linking them to V7; this is fixed above.

versions.untested_parts: No secure-code or insecure-code-for-a-class matched controls are evaluated, and no base-model misalignment rates are reported for the insecure-code comparisons.
The paper tests bad medical advice, risky financial advice and extreme-sports recommendations; it does not test reward hacks or number sequences.
A single rank-1 adapter is shown to induce misalignment, but the paper does not test whether one shared direction or persona feature mediates misalignment across fine-tunes.
No inoculation framing or brief benign retraining mitigation is tested.
The paper averages over three seeds rather than reporting seed-by-seed robustness. It tests models up to 32B parameters and does not test robustness beyond the stated model families and protocols.
